Theme

Conversation, family & daily routines

drama noun

a fuss, a scene made over something

also make a drama of, make a scene, make a fuss, fuss, a big fuss, kick up a fuss

classical

Cic. Mil. 18: quantās tragoediās excitat!
Cic. de Or. 2.205: tragoediās agāmus in nūgīs
Quint. 6.1.36: in parvīs lītibus tragoediās movēre (Lewis & Short)

tragoediae, tragoediārum f. pl.

noun, first declension; plural in this sense

a great to-do, high drama

Cicero’s figure from the stage: tragoediās excitāre, movēre, to raise a great commotion; tragoediās agere, to play the tragedian. In the singular a tragedy, and also a lofty, high-flown style (Lewis & Short).

Other words

  • turbae, turbārum f. pl. — a row, a scene, trouble

    noun, first declension · also used · classical · Plaut. Am. 476: turbās conciet; Caecil. ap. Non. 525.4: turbam aliquam dare (Lewis & Short)

    (in this sense mostly comic: Plaut., Ter.; in good prose rare (Lewis & Short))

    A row made by one or two people: turbās concīre (Plautus), turbam dare (Caecilius), to make a scene. Its everyday sense is a crowd (Lewis & Short).

Examples

  • nunc ejusdem Appiae nōmen quantās tragoediās excitat!

    and now what a drama the very name of the Appian Way stirs up!Cic. Mil. 18

  • sī aut tragoediās agāmus in nūgīs

    if we were to make a drama out of triflesCic. de Or. 2.205

  • nam Amphitruō āctūtum uxōrī turbās conciet

    for Amphitryon will make a scene with his wife straight awayPlaut. Am. 476

See also play, argument, be quiet.
